recommendation: Keep this commit as the FHIR-50710 source fix; allow the normal FHIR build/publication process to regenerate derived artifacts. No separate decision is needed here for FHIR-51195 or FHIR-53156 because they are related history, not unresolved parts of this seed.
issue_request: FHIR-50710 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 by BR&R and requested that listed ResearchStudy terminology bindings use THO ValueSets where available, with corresponding core CodeSystem and ValueSet definitions removed from the FHIR build.
initial_application: PR #3468 / commit 1b603c332e6c7b80b2bf02e2e6017689e8cab890 switched the listed ResearchStudy bindings to terminology.hl7.org ValueSet URLs and removed only the research-study-reason-stopped local terminology files, leaving artifact-relationship-type, research-study-prim-purp-type, research-study-phase, research-study-objective-type core XML definitions and one title-type example URI behind.
additional_context: BR&R 2025-05-27 minutes confirm approval of FHIR-50710. ResearchStudy and Composition are active resources in source/fhir.ini, so their resource-folder terminology XML files are current build source. Later FHIR-53156 ResearchStudy binding-strength work did not reverse the THO migration. Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Deleted the remaining stale core CodeSystem/ValueSet XML definitions for artifact-relationship-type, research-study-prim-purp-type, research-study-phase, and research-study-objective-type, and updated the CT.gov ResearchStudy example label.type coding system to http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/title-type. OID registry entries and generated-looking SVGs were intentionally left unchanged.
source_changes: Updated source/researchstudy/researchstudy-example-ctgov-study-record.xml to use the THO title-type CodeSystem URI
